newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish share suspension skews derivatives trading.
newsitem.headline: Spanish share suspension skews derivatives trading.

text.p: The suspension of trade in electrical groups Fecsa, Endesa and Sevillana on Friday distorted trade in Spanish futures and options, clashing with the expiry of October futures contracts.
Futures rose sharply after the announcement as traders speculated that the government would announce Endesa was taking over Fecsa and Sevillana.
The three shares have a heavy weighting in the Ibex-35 leading share index.
Their suspension complicates calculating the theoretical value of Ibex-35 futures, which is partly based on expectations about the future price movements of the shares in the index.

"The future embraces the capitalisation of the 35 Ibex shares. In theory, the value of the future would now adjust as if Endesa, Fecsa and Sevillana were trading unchanged, but in reality that's not the case," said Miguel Cuenca, head of stock derivatives trading at Credit Lyonnais in Madrid.

"What is happening is that people are making their guesses and calculations of possible rebounds or falls and are reflecting their expectations in the value of the future, so that the November reference will probably trade far off its theoretical value until the shares start trading again."
The market was discounting a rise of 15 points in the Ibex-35 index from around 4,350 once the electrical shares are quoted again.

Traders said the trading suspension had also cast uncertainty on October futures which expire this session, as it was uncertain whether they would start trading again before the liquidation price is set (between 1415 and 1445 GMT).

"The key is knowing whether the shares will resume trading today or not, and that's what people are betting on for the futures as well as the roll-over," said Alex Matitia, director of stock derivative trading at ODDO.
"The roll-over normally doesn't create much movement but this morning in one single moment we saw impressive jumps," said Cuenca.
Traders said the suspension of options on Endesa, Fecsa and Sevillana had also hit the market.
"People with options positions in one of the three shares won't be able to adjust until they are readmitted and there will surely be important price jumps when that happens," said Matitia.
